experiment.title: Within one window, does a broker's probe calls actually complete, or does a meaningful share fail?
experiment.note: Nothing in this record may change afterwards; a later change is a new, dated amendment, published first.

question: A broker that cannot be reached, or that errors out on a meaningful share of calls, cannot be routed to safely without a fallback -- regardless of what it would have billed or which provider it would have served from. Within one 7-day window, what fraction of identical, tiny probe calls to each broker complete successfully (an HTTP 200 response with a usable completion), and does any broker's failure rate cross a bar where a customer relying on that broker alone, with no fallback, would be taking on real, noticeable risk?
republication: This record republishes, by letter, a measurement already completed on a now-superseded branch (herd/exp024-broker-call-reliability-win, PR #310, closed) before this record existed: same window, same question, same decision rule, same result. It does not freeze a new hypothesis ahead of new data -- the window closed and was analysed before this record was written. What is new here is publishing by letter (the same decision EXP 015's own amendment-01 records) and a corrected arithmetic error a review found in the superseded branch, listed under corrections below.

window.rationale: The one remaining untouched week between EXP 015's window (ending 2026-11-04) and EXP 022's window (2026-11-11..2026-11-18).

capture.mechanism: Unchanged: the same scheduled capture workflow EXP 015 uses. No new capture code, no new key, no new spend.
capture.codeSha256Reference: Same files, same hashes as pinned in experiments/telemetry-truth/preregistration.json#/capture/sha256.
capture.anonymisation: Published rows are reduced by this record's own anonymise.mjs, the same reduction amendment-01 applies: broker to its letter (the same assignment EXP 015's amendment-01 uses), keyName's broker name to the same letter, and requestedModel/servedModel/servedProvider/estimateSource/the generation-record cross-check fields dropped -- this record's own metric never reads any of them.

metric.attempted: A row is 'attempted' for a broker if it is inside [window.from, window.to), has a broker field matching, and has a boolean ok field (this excludes the capture's own _header and _trailer summary rows, neither of which carries an ok field at all).
metric.failed: An attempted row with ok !== true. Its httpStatus (if present and not 200) and any error-shaped text field found on the row are recorded for transparency, but are descriptive only -- not part of the decision rule below.

decision.ruleNote: On the full 112 calls/broker/week (56 runs x 2 models) this window actually has, a 5% ceiling is 5.6 calls -- 'marginal' covers 1 to 5 failures, not 1 to 2. (A superseded branch of this record stated 'roughly 56 calls/broker/week, that is 1-2 failed calls', confusing the per-model run count with the per-broker call count; corrected here, see corrections below. Broker X's verdict in the result is unaffected either way: 1 failure is marginal under both readings.)

perBroker.notEnoughCalls: callsAttempted below minCalls: reported as 'not enough calls', never classified either way.
perBroker.reliable: failureRate === 0. Every attempted call in-window completed.
perBroker.marginal: 0 < failureRate <= 0.05. At least one failure, but not enough to call the broker unreliable on this window alone.
perBroker.unreliable: failureRate > 0.05. A customer routing to this broker alone, with no fallback, would have noticed real failures this week.

stoppingRule: A single pre-registered 7-day window, not a cadence. No additional counted window is triggered by an 'unreliable' or 'marginal' result; a periodic recheck would be its own, separately pre-registered follow-up.
cost: $0 marginal. The capture workflow already runs every 3 hours regardless of this record; this record only adds one analysis pass over already-collected rows. No new broker calls, no new keys, no new spend.

analysis.check: node experiments/broker-call-reliability/analyse.mjs --check exits 0 only if results.json is exactly what the frozen script computes from the committed inputs.

reviewNote: Two adversarial reviews with distinct lenses, same discipline as every other record in this repository, before this record's PR is called ready.
corrections: A superseded branch of this record (herd/exp024-broker-call-reliability-win, PR #310, closed) named all three brokers directly in results.json and every capture row -- this record never does.

That superseded branch's decision.ruleNote said 'roughly 56 calls/broker/week, that is 1-2 failed calls' for the 5% marginal ceiling. The real per-broker volume is 112 calls/week (56 runs x 2 models), which the same record's own calibration already stated; 5% of 112 is 5.6, so 'marginal' covers 1 to 5 failures, not 1 to 2. Corrected in decision.ruleNote above. The one broker that failed once in this window is marginal under either reading, so the result is unaffected.
That superseded branch's commit message named an internal lane; this one does not.
limits: Tiny, uncached, list-priced calls on two models, three brokers, one week.
A revoked or missing key produces fewer rows, not a row with ok:false -- this record's callsAttempted counts only what is actually present in the capture.
One week is a snapshot, not a trend.
